understands that in the division of

121	the Holy Land, as it is called, there is
a divine matter in this, a spiritual matter. It is a matter that touches each

122	one in his own soul.

123	The division is not only the division of land, where the people of
Israel each received his portion. It is in fact

124	the division of the mission of each one. Each tribe had
its own special mission, each family its

125	special mission, and each and every one has
this special mission. And this is the wonderful message

126	that HaShem performed this wondrous miracle,
which gives us the picture

127	of how we will know what our mission is and how we will behave
and live with our mission.

128	But let us first set out a preface.

129	We know that no two people are the same. Just as
their faces are not alike, their opinions are not alike.

130	Their character traits are not alike, and the fingerprints are not
alike, the fingerprints of ours, which are one centimeter.

131	And let us see something wonderful: in that one centimeter,
how many possibilities there can be. There were never two people, and there will not be, among the billions upon billions of

132	people who exist and who have existed, who have

133	two identical fingerprints. A wonder of wonders.

134	And so it is very important that each one of us

135	be aware of his special qualities.

136	He needs to know the gift that HaShem gave him. And I
know there are people who, out of humility, say: I have nothing,

137	no, no, no, no, that is not true, it is the opposite.

138	The moment you are not aware of your gifts, it is ingratitude.

139	HaShem gave you the gifts. HaShem gave you a good mind,

140	a good heart, sensitivity,

141	a sense

142	of helping others, a sense of prayer, whatever it is, and you

143	do not thank HaShem. This has nothing to do with
pride, since you did not make this yourself. Do not take

144	credit for it.

145	It is not credit for you. It obligates you
to act. HaShem gave you the strength, you need

146	to use it.

147	There is a saying I heard in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, I did not see
it written, that he says: what is Gehinnom?

148	Gehinnom is a state where a person goes after 120 years
up

149	to Heaven

150	and sees what he could have been, what he could
have done, the enormous potential he had,

151	and suddenly he feels: I wasted this, I threw it
in the trash. That is the greatest Gehinnom. And so each one

152	must be aware and have the perception,
the grasp, of what my qualities are. I think that once

153	I told this about the Rebe Rashab, a great-grandfather of the Rebbe.

154	The Rebbe Rashab once had a farbrengen and spoke words of
immense wisdom, and then someone said to him: Rashab, you are

155	so profound, so wise, have you ever made a mistake
in your life? He says: yes. In what did you make a mistake? He says:

156	in my qualities. I say to him: you have many
qualities, do not be humble, you have many qualities. He says:

157	no, no, you did not understand me. I did not mean
that I made a mistake by thinking I have many qualities

158	and I do not. The opposite. I thought I had fewer, and I have
more. The Rebbe Rashab said this to his son. This is the way of

159	Chassidut: know your qualities, but know that it
obligates you. And this is what is written: Jacob saw a ladder

160	set on the earth, its top reaching heaven. And behold, angels of

161	God ascending and descending on it.

162	The commentators ask: it should have been the opposite. Behold, the
angels of God descending, they are in heaven,

163	and afterwards ascending. What is the meaning of ascending and descending?

164	So the Midrash says: they ascended on high to the lofty levels,
and they saw that Jacob's image is engraved

165	on the Throne of Glory.

166	They descend below and see him sleeping.

167	The ministering angels sought to harm Jacob.

168	They see him as he could be,

169	and they look here, and with their own eyes they did not see
his greatness. So how do you miss such

170	potential, such an enormous potential that HaShem gave him?

171	That is to say, each one must be aware,
aware of what you can be, of your potential.

172	And this is not the time to be humble: I have nothing, I am
not successful, I cannot. The opposite. "And his heart was lifted

173	in the ways of HaShem": be aware of this and thank
HaShem. There is a verse: "Honor HaShem

174	with your substance."

175	From what He graced you with.

176	You need to honor HaShem, to use
what He graced you with, what He gave you.

177	So the Midrash says: He gave you a son, make for him a brit
milah. He gave you a house, make the mezuzah. He gave you

178	a courtyard, make a sukkah.

179	The Midrash says: if you have a pleasant voice,

180	rise and say Shema Yisrael aloud and be
a chazan.

181	You need to honor HaShem with your substance. What is "your substance"?
What He truly graced you with. Each one must think about

182	his qualities. And not only that: if he does not know,
ask your good friend. Ask about your qualities.

183	And with us, we have

184	a yeshiva of young men,

185	and many times I gather them and I say: each
one write three or five qualities about his friend.

186	When you tell him to write about himself, he is shy.
Write about your friend. And afterwards each one gives the

187	letter to his neighbor, and people open up so much,
they receive so much

188	strength and power.

189	The Gemara comes and says, Resh Lakish: the world was not
fit to use gold. Why is gold needed in the world? One needs

190	food, one needs water. Why is gold needed? Why was it created?
For the Mishkan, or it is written, for the Beit HaMikdash.

191	The Rebbe says a wonderful thing:

192	gold, in essence, is a luxury. You do not need
it in order to live.

193	There are things a person needs

194	in the world in order to live: intellect, heart, health, and so on
and so on. But every person needs to think: what do I have
that is a luxury? Gold is a luxury.

195	What thing do I have above average,

196	above what a person needs in order to live?
